met_analysis:
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood persists and now extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Ferozepur, Dehradun, Shahjahanpur, Varanasi, Dehri, centre of Depression over Jharkhand and adjoining northern parts of Gangetic West Bengal and Digha & thence southeastwards to Northeast Bay of Bengal and extends upto 0.9 km above mean sea level with embedded cyclonic circulations over north Haryana & neighbourhood and East Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood.
A trough runs from the cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh to Gujarat across north Madhya Pradesh and southeast Rajasthan at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northwest Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level merged with the above trough.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Jammu Division & neighbourhood now lies over Punjab & neighbourhood at 5.8 km above mean sea level with a trough aloft at its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level runs roughly along Long. 75°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
The Shear Zone roughly along Lat. 22°N across central & adjoining north Peninsular India between 3.1 & 9.6 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
